title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 11
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt: A graph showing quarterly revenue in the retail sales sector presents the following data: Q1: $2.4M, Q2: $3.1M, Q3: $2.8M, Q4: $3.6M. According to the graph, which segment/period shows the highest value?
options: B. The value closest to the overall average
C. Cannot be determined from the data
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret retail sales data on quarterly revenue.

questions.prompt: Based on the chart of patient wait times data (Emergency: 45min, Outpatient: 28min, Radiology: 62min, Laboratory: 19min), which TWO values would combine to equal approximately the average?
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret hospital operations data on patient wait times.

questions.prompt: A scatter plot comparing application success rates across university admissions categories shows: Engineering: 12%, Business: 18%, Arts: 25%, Sciences: 15%, Law: 9%. If the trend continued, which projection is most consistent?
options: D. The value closest to the overall average
E. Cannot be determined from the data
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret university admissions data on application success rates.

questions.prompt: A graph showing delivery performance in the logistics sector presents the following data: On-time: 78%, Early: 8%, Late <1 day: 10%, Late >1 day: 4%. According to the graph, which segment/period shows the highest value?
questions.explanation: This graphics_interpretation question tests ability to interpret logistics data on delivery performance.

dataContext.data: On-time: 78%, Early: 8%, Late <1 day: 10%, Late >1 day: 4%

questions.prompt: Analysis of engagement metrics in social media: Likes per post: 340, Shares: 89, Comments: 47, Click-through: 6.2%. Select the value closest to the median AND the value that represents the greatest deviation from the mean.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret social media data on engagement metrics.

dataContext.data: Likes per post: 340, Shares: 89, Comments: 47, Click-through: 6.2%

questions.prompt: Given energy consumption monthly utility costs data: Jan: $4,200, Apr: $2,900, Jul: $5,800, Oct: $3,100. In the left column select the highest-performing category; in the right column select the category that improved most year-over-year.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret energy consumption data on monthly utility costs.

questions.prompt: A employee performance manager reviews training completion rates: Sales: 91%, Operations: 73%, HR: 88%, Finance: 95%, IT: 82%. Select: (1) the category requiring immediate attention and (2) the category that exceeds the target of the average by the greatest margin.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret employee performance data on training completion rates.

questions.prompt: Analysis of property price indices in real estate: City centre: 148, Suburbs: 112, Rural: 89, Coastal: 167. Select the value closest to the median AND the value that represents the greatest deviation from the mean.
questions.explanation: This two_part_analysis question tests ability to interpret real estate data on property price indices.

questions.prompt: Three data sources on pharmaceutical clinical trial outcomes are provided: (Memo) Overall performance improved this quarter. (Table) Complete response: 34%, Partial response: 28%, Stable disease: 21%, Progression: 17%. (Email) Stakeholders express concern about outliers. Which source most directly supports the memo's claim?
options: A. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret pharmaceutical data on clinical trial outcomes.

dataContext.data: Complete response: 34%, Partial response: 28%, Stable disease: 21%, Progression: 17%

questions.prompt: Source 1 (Report): airline operations on-time performance by route shows: Domestic short: 88%, Domestic long: 79%, International: 71%, Regional: 84%. Source 2 (Email): The weakest performer needs a 20% improvement to meet targets. Source 3 (Table): Targets are set at the top-quartile value. Which category needs improvement?
options: B. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret airline operations data on on-time performance by route.

dataContext.data: Domestic short: 88%, Domestic long: 79%, International: 71%, Regional: 84%

questions.prompt: Reviewing food service records: Source A shows customer satisfaction scores: Food quality: 4.2/5, Service speed: 3.8/5, Value: 3.9/5, Ambiance: 4.1/5. Source B notes the average. Source C flags values more than 25% above or below average. Which values would Source C flag?
options: C. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret food service data on customer satisfaction scores.

dataContext.data: Food quality: 4.2/5, Service speed: 3.8/5, Value: 3.9/5, Ambiance: 4.1/5

questions.prompt: Three data sources on manufacturing defect rates by production line are provided: (Memo) Overall performance improved this quarter. (Table) Line A: 0.8%, Line B: 1.4%, Line C: 0.5%, Line D: 2.1%. (Email) Stakeholders express concern about outliers. Which source most directly supports the memo's claim?
options: D. All three sources are equally relevant
questions.explanation: This multi_source_reasoning question tests ability to interpret manufacturing data on defect rates by production line.

dataContext.data: Line A: 0.8%, Line B: 1.4%, Line C: 0.5%, Line D: 2.1%

questions.prompt: What is the relative ranking of categories in banking loan approval rates? (1) Personal: 64%. (2) The remaining values follow a consistent trend.
options: A. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
B. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
C. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
D. Each statement alone is sufficient
E. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret banking data on loan approval rates.

questions.prompt: Is the marketing campaign conversion rates above the industry benchmark of the median? (1) Email: 3.2%. (2) The range of all values is 6.1%.
options: A. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
B. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
C. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
D. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
E. Each statement alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret marketing data on campaign conversion rates.

questions.prompt: Can the average telecommunications subscriber churn rates be calculated precisely? (1) Postpaid: 2.1%, Prepaid: 8.4%, Broadband: 1.7%, Enterprise: 0.8%. (2) All categories are measured using the same methodology.
options: A. Each statement alone is sufficient
B. Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
C. Statement (1) alone is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient
D. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
E. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: This data_sufficiency question tests ability to interpret telecommunications data on subscriber churn rates.

questions.prompt: What is the relative ranking of categories in education student assessment pass rates? (1) Mathematics: 73%. (2) The remaining values follow a consistent trend.
options: A. Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is sufficient
B. Each statement alone is sufficient

E. Statement (2) alone is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient
